# Physics equations — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/physics-equations.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/physics-equations.ttl`](../decks/physics-equations.ttl) · **Cards:** 42 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

42 fundamental equations of school and first-year university physics: motion and forces, energy, work and power, gravitation, oscillations, fluids, heat and gases, waves and optics, electricity and magnetism, and photons and relativity. Front: the law or quantity, naming every symbol, e.g. "Ohm's law: voltage U across a resistance R carrying a current I"; back: the equation, e.g. "U = RI". Voltage is U throughout, as in Swedish schools. Each equation is checked for dimensional consistency with SymPy and against OpenStax University Physics, and where they state it, against Wikidata and Swedish Wikipedia.

## Licensing

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its content comes from two sources whose licences allow anything: the compiler's own selection, wording, choice of symbols, notation and SymPy checks (dedicated to the public domain with the deck; the equations are laws of physics and definitions, which are not copyrightable in any case) and Wikidata (structured data under CC0), from which the English and Swedish names of the quantities and laws and the quantity symbols were taken and against whose defining formulas cards were compared. OpenStax University Physics (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, recorded as all rights reserved because the builder has no identifier for a non-commercial licence) and the Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used only to verify the equations and the Swedish terms: no text, notation, table layout or list was copied from them; single established terms (periodtid, lyftkraft, svartkropp, brytningslagen, tvärsnittsarea) carry no protectable expression. The selection follows the standard syllabus, which the subject dictates, and was made independently of any list. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence remain under their sources' licences and are not part of the CC0 deck.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (SymPy, live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. Selection: the equations a Swedish upper-secondary course (Fysik 1 and 2) and a first university course in physics ask students to know were listed from general knowledge of the subject, following the brief of the library editor (Newton's second law, weight, momentum, kinetic and potential energy, work, power, Ohm's law, electric power, Coulomb's law, the law of gravitation, pressure, density, wave speed, Snell's law, E = mc², the ideal gas law and others of the same rank); no list was copied from any source. Each was kept only if it has one standard form and the front can name every symbol so that exactly one equation answers it (see the selection for what was left out and why).
3. Symbols: one symbol set is used throughout and every front names each symbol it uses, in English and in Swedish. The brief noted that Swedish schools write U for voltage while English texts often write V; the deck uses U (Ohm's law U = RI, electric power P = UI, capacitance C = Q/U), which is also the quantity symbol that Wikidata gives first for voltage (Q25428, P416 "U" and "V"), and the Ohm's law card's note gives the English form V = IR. Other choices: s for distance and displacement, v₀ for the initial velocity, Eₖ and Eₚ for kinetic and potential energy (as Swedish texts write them; OpenStax writes K and U), F for every force including weight and buoyancy, Q for both charge and heat, T for both period and absolute temperature, ρ for both density and resistivity, h for both height and the Planck constant, k for both the spring constant and the Coulomb constant (the front of each card says which is meant), and capital L for every length, because a lower-case l is easily read as the capital I of the current in "F = BIl". Magnitudes are used throughout (no vector arrows); where a direction or an angle matters, the front says so ("perpendicular", "in the direction of the force") and a note gives the general form.
4. Notation of the backs: the whole equation, subject first ("F = ma", "v² = v₀² + 2as"), as one text in no language (tagged zxx) shared by both languages. Plain Unicode: superscripts ² and ⁴, subscripts ₀ ₁ ₂ ₖ ₚ, Greek letters, √ with parentheses, a slash for division (mv²/2 rather than ½mv², so that every back uses one style; the ½ form is named in a note where it is common) and − (U+2212) for minus in the notes.
5. Machine verification (query 9): verify_physics.py, run with `uv run --with sympy python3 verify_physics.py <dossier>` (SymPy 1.14.0), reads the back of every card from the dossier and parses its own text into a SymPy equation (so the check runs on what the card says, not on a retyped copy). (a) Dimensional consistency: every symbol is replaced by the SI unit of the quantity the front names (the gravitational, Coulomb, molar gas, Stefan–Boltzmann and Planck constants and the speed of light by SymPy's own definitions of those constants, sympy.physics.units), and every additive term of the equation must reduce to the same SI base dimensions; all 42 cards pass. (b) Derivation: for 18 cards a short derivation from first principles is substituted and the difference of the two sides must simplify to 0: the three equations of constant acceleration (by integrating a and v), kinetic energy (work–energy integral), potential energy (work against mg), centripetal force (differentiating uniform circular motion), the periods of the pendulum (small-angle equation) and the spring (both solved with dsolve), hydrostatic pressure (weight of a column over its base), Archimedes' principle (pressure difference on a submerged box), resistors in series and in parallel (Kirchhoff), Snell's law (Fermat's least time), electric power (P = W/t with W = QU and Q = It), the force on a conductor (summing QvB over the charge carriers), wave speed, weight (F = ma with a = g) and the de Broglie relation (consistency for a photon); all 18 pass. (c) Negative controls: 11 deliberately wrong equations (Eₖ = mv, T = 2π√(g/L), F = Gm₁m₂/r, E = mc, P = σAT³, F = kQ₁Q₂/r, T = 2π√(k/m), and for the derivations Eₖ = mv², s = v₀t + at², R = R₁ + R₂ for parallel resistors and n₁ sin θ₂ = n₂ sin θ₁) must fail, and all 11 do. A dimensional check cannot see a wrong numerical factor (Eₖ = mv² passes it, as the script records); the remaining 24 cards, which are definitions or laws without a derivation in the script, rest on the dimensional check and the source comparisons in steps 6–8. The result of every card is quoted in its evidence (the "derivation" source).
6. OpenStax: the tables of contents of University Physics volumes 1–3 were read from the OpenStax archive (os_toc.py, query 5) and the Key Equations pages of 21 chapters and 14 sections were downloaded (os_fetch.py, query 6, recorded verbatim). os_fetch.py turns the MathML of each page into linear text (fractions as (a)/(b), powers as x^2, subscripts as x_0, vectors as a letter followed by a combining arrow); each card's evidence quotes that text, and make_dossier.py confirmed that each quote occurs verbatim in the saved page text. Every card's equation agrees with OpenStax, up to the symbol convention (OpenStax writes V for voltage, q for charge, K and U for kinetic and potential energy, w for weight, d for distance) and up to rearrangement where OpenStax states the same relation solved for another quantity (F = QE for E = F/Q) or in a more general form (p = p₀ + ρgh, F = IlB sin θ, F = qvB sin θ, W = Fd cos θ, Coulomb's law with 1/(4πε₀)); these differences are listed in round 0 of quality control. OpenStax is used for verification only (licence CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
7. Wikidata: the items of the quantities and laws were found with wbsearchentities (wd_search.py, query 2) and their English and Swedish labels and aliases, quantity symbols (P416) and defining formulas (P2534, TeX) were fetched with wbgetentities (wd_get.py, query 3). Every card's evidence quotes the items concerned, generated from the saved response by make_dossier.py. 27 cards have a P2534 formula on one of their items that states the card's relation, an equivalent of it or its instantaneous or vector form; none disagrees (the forms differ in letters, vector notation or arrangement, e.g. Snell's law as the ratio sin θ₁/sin θ₂ = n₂/n₁, the Stefan–Boltzmann law per unit area as M_b = σT⁴, kinetic energy as T = ½mv²). For the other 15 cards Wikidata states no formula of the relation, so only the names and symbols on their fronts are checked against it. The builder cannot check P2534 itself, because the SPARQL endpoint returns that datatype rendered as MathML, so its checks (102 in all) are label and alias checks of the English and Swedish names on the fronts and P416 checks of the quantity symbols F, m, ρ, V, f, n, U, R, I, Q and B.
8. Swedish text: the Swedish fronts and notes were written directly in Swedish, using the Wikidata Swedish labels and aliases of the quantities and laws (step 7) and the usage of Swedish Wikipedia: fetch_wiki.py (query 7) downloaded the current wikitext and revision id of 38 Swedish articles, wiki_lines.py and sv_terms.py (query 8) listed the lines stating each formula and the occurrences of the Swedish terms that are not Wikidata labels (medelfart, medelacceleration, starthastighet, resulterande kraft, medeleffekt, fjäderkonstant, matematisk pendel, periodtid, lyftkraft, svartkropp, brytningslagen, infallsvinkel, brytningsvinkel, punktladdning, Coulombs konstant, seriekopplade, parallellkopplade, tvärsnittsarea, kondensator, viloenergi). 39 cards quote the Swedish article that states their equation, with a link to the revision (for the Stefan–Boltzmann law its general form with emissivity and surroundings, for average acceleration its form a = (v − v₀)/t, for the spring's period the angular frequency ω = √(k/m), from which T = 2π/ω); the three others (heat and temperature change, the force on a conductor, photon energy; see quality control) rest on OpenStax, Wikidata and the derivation. Swedish conventions: decimal comma in the Coulomb constant's note, "de Broglie-våglängden" with a lower-case particle as Wikidata's label "de Broglie-våg", and "Allmänna gaslagen" (the Swedish school name, a Wikidata alias) rather than the label "Ideala gaslagen".
9. Finally make_dossier.py wrote this dossier from the card list, the saved source data and the script's results; the builder (python3 scripts/authored_decks.py build physics-equations) ran the Wikidata checks against live Wikidata and wrote the deck and this report, and the deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (node scripts/validate_sources.ts physics-equations). The helper scripts other than verify_physics.py and os_fetch.py are not published with the deck; what they do is described above.

## Selection

Included: 42 equations of school and first-year university physics, one card each: kinematics (average speed and acceleration, the three equations of constant acceleration), dynamics (Newton's second law, weight, momentum, Hooke's law, the law of gravitation, centripetal force), energy (kinetic and gravitational potential energy, work, power), oscillations and waves (periods of the simple pendulum and of a mass on a spring, frequency, wave speed), fluids (pressure, density, hydrostatic pressure, Archimedes' principle), heat (the ideal gas law, heat and temperature change, the Stefan–Boltzmann law), optics (Snell's law, refractive index), electricity and magnetism (Ohm's law, electric power, current, Coulomb's law, electric field strength, resistors in series and in parallel, resistivity, capacitance, the magnetic force on a conductor and on a moving charge) and modern physics (photon energy, mass–energy equivalence, the de Broglie wavelength). Every front names each symbol so that one equation answers it; the deck is studied front to back only, because a back such as F = ma cannot ask for one law. Left out: the impulse (J in English texts, I in Swedish ones, which clashes with the current), torque (τ in English, M in Swedish), the thin-lens and mirror equations (the sign conventions differ between textbooks: 1/f = 1/a + 1/b with real-is-positive distances, 1/f = 1/v − 1/u in the Cartesian convention), the first law of thermodynamics (the sign of the work differs between physics and chemistry texts), Kepler's laws, induction (Faraday's law with its sign) and other equations beyond most first courses; general forms with vectors, angles or integrals are given in the notes where they help (W = Fs cos θ, F = BIL sin θ, F = −kx, p₀ + ρgh).

```
"""Download OpenStax University Physics pages and print their key equations / chosen equations as linear text.

Usage: python3 os_fetch.py v1:3-key-equations v2:9-key-equations ...
Each page is saved as openstax/<vol>-<slug>.html. MathML is linearised by mathml_text():
mi/mn/mo text concatenated, msub as base_sub, msup as base^sup, mfrac as (num)/(den), msqrt as √(…),
munderover/mover as base with the accent ignored for vectors (→ shown after the letter).
"""
import re, sys, time, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET
H = Path(__file__).parent
UA = {"User-Agent": "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"}
BOOK = {"v1": "university-physics-volume-1", "v2": "university-physics-volume-2", "v3": "university-physics-volume-3"}


def lin(e):
    tag = e.tag.split('}')[-1]
    kids = [k for k in e if k.tag.split('}')[-1] != 'annotation-xml']
    if tag in ('mi', 'mn', 'mo', 'mtext', 'ms'):
        return (e.text or '').strip()
    if tag == 'annotation-xml' or tag == 'annotation':
        return ''
    if tag == 'msub':
        return lin(kids[0]) + '_' + wrap(lin(kids[1]))
    if tag == 'msup':
        return lin(kids[0]) + '^' + wrap(lin(kids[1]))
    if tag == 'msubsup':
        return lin(kids[0]) + '_' + wrap(lin(kids[1])) + '^' + wrap(lin(kids[2]))
    if tag == 'mfrac':
        return '(' + lin(kids[0]) + ')/(' + lin(kids[1]) + ')'
    if tag == 'msqrt':
        return '√(' + ''.join(lin(k) for k in kids) + ')'
    if tag == 'mroot':
        return 'root(' + lin(kids[0]) + ',' + lin(kids[1]) + ')'
    if tag in ('mover', 'munder', 'munderover'):
        base = lin(kids[0])
        rest = ''.join(lin(k) for k in kids[1:])
        return base + ('⃗' if rest == '→' else ('^' + rest if rest else ''))
    return ''.join(lin(k) for k in kids)


def wrap(s):
    return s if len(s) <= 1 else '{' + s + '}'


def mathml_text(m):
    m = re.sub(r'&nbsp;', ' ', m)
    m = re.sub(r'\s(xmlns(:\w+)?)="[^"]*"', '', m)
    try:
        return lin(ET.fromstring(m))
    except ET.ParseError as ex:
        return '[unparsed]'


def page_text(html):
    body = re.sub(r'<script.*?</script>', '', html, flags=re.S)
    body = re.sub(r'<math\b.*?</math>', lambda mo: ' ⟦' + mathml_text(mo.group(0)) + '⟧ ', body, flags=re.S)
    body = re.sub(r'<(tr|p|li|h\d|div)\b[^>]*>', '\n', body)
    body = re.sub(r'<t[dh]\b[^>]*>', ' | ', body)
    body = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', body)
    body = re.sub(r'[ \t]+', ' ', body)
    return '\n'.join(l.strip() for l in body.splitlines() if l.strip())


if __name__ == '__main__':
    (H / 'openstax').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    for arg in sys.argv[1:]:
        vol, slug = arg.split(':')
        f = H / 'openstax' / f'{vol}-{slug}.html'
        if not f.exists():
            url = f'https://openstax.org/books/{BOOK[vol]}/pages/{slug}'
            f.write_bytes(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers=UA)).read())
            time.sleep(1)
        t = page_text(f.read_text())
        (H / 'openstax' / f'{vol}-{slug}.txt').write_text(t)
        print('=====', arg)

```

**7. Wikitext and revision id of the Swedish articles (python3 <scratch>/fetch_wiki.py sv "Fart" "Acceleration" "Likformigt accelererad rörelse" "Newtons rörelselagar" "Tyngd" "Rörelsemängd" "Kinetisk energi" "Potentiell energi" "Arbete (fysik)" "Effekt" "Hookes lag" "Newtons gravitationslag" "Centripetalkraft" "Matematisk pendel" "Pendel" "Harmonisk oscillator" "Tryck" "Densitet" "Hydrostatiskt tryck" "Arkimedes princip" "Ideala gaslagen" "Specifik värmekapacitet" "Stefan–Boltzmanns lag" "Frekvens" "Våglängd" "Snells lag" "Brytningsindex" "Ohms lag" "Elektrisk effekt" "Elektrisk ström" "Coulombs lag" "Elektriskt fält" "Seriekoppling" "Parallellkoppling" "Elektrisk resistivitet" "Kapacitans" "Lorentzkraft" "Foton" "E = mc²" "De Broglie-våglängd" "Materievåg" "Periodtid" "Fjäderkonstant" "Resistans" "Elektrisk spänning"; three titles do not exist and several redirect, giving 38 distinct articles)** (Swedish Wikipedia: articles on the quantities and laws)

**9. Machine verification of every card with SymPy (uv run --with sympy python3 <scratch>/verify_physics.py <dossier>); the script, verbatim:** (Derivations and SymPy checks for the Solid Memo physics equations deck)

```
"""Machine-check every card of the "physics-equations" deck with SymPy.

Run: uv run --with sympy python3 verify_physics.py <dossier.json>

1. The back of every card (plain Unicode, e.g. "Eₖ = mv²/2") is parsed into a SymPy
   equation by parse_back(), so the check runs on the card's own text, not a copy.
2. Dimensional check (sympy.physics.units, SI): every symbol is replaced by the SI unit
   of the quantity the front names (UNITS below; the constants G, k, R, σ, h, c by
   SymPy's own definitions of those constants), and every additive term of
   lhs − rhs must reduce to the same SI base dimensions.
3. Derivation check, for the cards where a short first-principles derivation exists
   (DERIVE below): the derived value is substituted and lhs − rhs must simplify to 0.
4. Negative controls: deliberately wrong equations must fail the check meant to catch them.
Results are written to verify_results.json next to this script.
"""
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import sympy as sp
from sympy.parsing.sympy_parser import parse_expr
from sympy.physics import units as u
from sympy.physics.units import Dimension
from sympy.physics.units.systems.si import SI, dimsys_SI

H = Path(__file__).parent

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- parsing
SUP = {"²": "**2", "³": "**3", "⁴": "**4"}
SUB = {"₀": "0", "₁": "1", "₂": "2", "ₖ": "k", "ₚ": "p"}
GREEK = {"ρ": "rho", "λ": "lam", "σ": "sigma", "θ": "theta", "ε": "eps"}


def tokens(s):
    out, i = [], 0
    while i < len(s):
        ch = s[i]
        if ch == " ":
            i += 1
        elif s.startswith("sin", i):
            out.append(("fn", "sin"))
            i += 3
        elif ch == "√":
            out.append(("fn", "sqrt"))
            i += 1
        elif ch in SUP:
            out.append(("sup", SUP[ch]))
            i += 1
        elif ch in SUB:
            kind, name = out.pop()
            out.append((kind, name + SUB[ch]))
            i += 1
        elif ch == "Δ":
            nxt = GREEK.get(s[i + 1], s[i + 1])
            out.append(("id", "Delta_" + nxt))
            i += 2
        elif ch == "π":
            out.append(("num", "pi"))
            i += 1
        elif ch in GREEK or ch.isalpha():
            out.append(("id", GREEK.get(ch, ch)))
            i += 1
        elif ch.isdigit():
            j = i
            while j < len(s) and s[j].isdigit():
                j += 1
            out.append(("num", s[i:j]))
            i = j
        elif ch in "+−-=/()":
            out.append(("op", {"−": "-"}.get(ch, ch)))
            i += 1
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} in {s!r}")
    return out


def to_python(s):
    toks = tokens(s)
    py, prev_end = [], False
    i = 0
    while i < len(toks):
        kind, v = toks[i]
        starts = kind in ("id", "num", "fn") or (kind == "op" and v == "(")
        if prev_end and starts:
            py.append("*")
        if kind == "fn" and v == "sin" and toks[i + 1][0] == "id":
            py.append(f"sin({toks[i + 1][1]})")
            i += 2
            prev_end = True
            continue
        py.append(v)
        prev_end = kind in ("id", "num", "sup") or (kind == "op" and v == ")")
        i += 1
    return "".join(py)


def parse_back(s):
    lhs, rhs = to_python(s).split("=")
    names = set(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*", lhs + " " + rhs)) - {"sin", "sqrt", "pi"}
    local = {n: sp.Symbol(n, positive=True) for n in names}
    local.update({"sin": sp.sin, "sqrt": sp.sqrt, "pi": sp.pi})
    glob = {"Integer": sp.Integer, "Symbol": sp.Symbol, "Float": sp.Float, "Rational": sp.Rational}
    return (parse_expr(lhs, local_dict=local, global_dict=glob), parse_expr(rhs, local_dict=local, global_dict=glob),
            local)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- units
m_, s_, kg, N, J, W, Pa = u.meter, u.second, u.kilogram, u.newton, u.joule, u.watt, u.pascal
K, mol, C, A, V, ohm, F, T, Hz = u.kelvin, u.mole, u.coulomb, u.ampere, u.volt, u.ohm, u.farad, u.tesla, u.hertz
UNITS = {
    "average-speed": {"v": m_ / s_, "s": m_, "t": s_},
    "average-acceleration": {"a": m_ / s_**2, "Delta_v": m_ / s_, "Delta_t": s_},
    "velocity-constant-acceleration": {"v": m_ / s_, "v0": m_ / s_, "a": m_ / s_**2, "t": s_},
    "displacement-constant-acceleration": {"s": m_, "v0": m_ / s_, "a": m_ / s_**2, "t": s_},
    "velocity-displacement": {"v": m_ / s_, "v0": m_ / s_, "a": m_ / s_**2, "s": m_},
    "newtons-second-law": {"F": N, "m": kg, "a": m_ / s_**2},
    "weight": {"F": N, "m": kg, "g": m_ / s_**2},
    "momentum": {"p": kg * m_ / s_, "m": kg, "v": m_ / s_},
    "kinetic-energy": {"Ek": J, "m": kg, "v": m_ / s_},
    "potential-energy": {"Ep": J, "m": kg, "g": m_ / s_**2, "h": m_},
    "work": {"W": J, "F": N, "s": m_},
    "power": {"P": W, "W": J, "t": s_},
    "hookes-law": {"F": N, "k": N / m_, "x": m_},
    "gravitation": {"F": N, "G": u.gravitational_constant, "m1": kg, "m2": kg, "r": m_},
    "centripetal-force": {"F": N, "m": kg, "v": m_ / s_, "r": m_},
    "pendulum-period": {"T": s_, "L": m_, "g": m_ / s_**2},
    "spring-period": {"T": s_, "m": kg, "k": N / m_},
    "pressure": {"p": Pa, "F": N, "A": m_**2},
    "density": {"rho": kg / m_**3, "m": kg, "V": m_**3},
    "hydrostatic-pressure": {"p": Pa, "rho": kg / m_**3, "g": m_ / s_**2, "h": m_},
    "archimedes-principle": {"F": N, "rho": kg / m_**3, "V": m_**3, "g": m_ / s_**2},
    "ideal-gas-law": {"p": Pa, "V": m_**3, "n": mol, "R": u.molar_gas_constant, "T": K},
    "heat-and-temperature": {"Q": J, "m": kg, "c": J / (kg * K), "Delta_T": K},
    "stefan-boltzmann-law": {"P": W, "sigma": u.stefan_boltzmann_constant, "A": m_**2, "T": K},
    "frequency-and-period": {"f": Hz, "T": s_},
    "wave-speed": {"v": m_ / s_, "f": Hz, "lam": m_},
    "snells-law": {"n1": 1, "n2": 1, "theta1": u.radian, "theta2": u.radian},
    "refractive-index": {"n": 1, "c": u.speed_of_light, "v": m_ / s_},
    "ohms-law": {"U": V, "R": ohm, "I": A},
    "electric-power": {"P": W, "U": V, "I": A},
    "electric-current": {"I": A, "Q": C, "t": s_},
    "coulombs-law": {"F": N, "k": u.coulomb_constant, "Q1": C, "Q2": C, "r": m_},
    "electric-field-strength": {"E": V / m_, "F": N, "Q": C},
    "resistors-in-series": {"R": ohm, "R1": ohm, "R2": ohm},
    "resistors-in-parallel": {"R": ohm, "R1": ohm, "R2": ohm},
    "resistance-and-resistivity": {"R": ohm, "rho": ohm * m_, "L": m_, "A": m_**2},
    "capacitance": {"C": F, "Q": C, "U": V},
    "force-on-current-carrying-conductor": {"F": N, "B": T, "I": A, "L": m_},
    "force-on-moving-charge": {"F": N, "Q": C, "v": m_ / s_, "B": T},
    "photon-energy": {"E": J, "h": u.planck, "f": Hz},
    "mass-energy-equivalence": {"E": J, "m": kg, "c": u.speed_of_light},
    "de-broglie-wavelength": {"lam": m_, "h": u.planck, "p": kg * m_ / s_},
}
BASE = ["mass", "length", "time", "current", "temperature", "amount_of_substance"]
SHORT = {"mass": "M", "length": "L", "time": "T", "current": "I", "temperature": "Θ", "amount_of_substance": "N"}
SUPS = str.maketrans("-0123456789", "⁻⁰¹²³⁴⁵⁶⁷⁸⁹")


def dims(term, units, local):
    q = term.subs({local[k]: v for k, v in units.items() if k in local})
    deps = dimsys_SI.get_dimensional_dependencies(Dimension(SI.get_dimensional_expr(q)))
    return {str(k.name): v for k, v in deps.items()}


def fmt(d):
    parts = [SHORT[b] + ("" if d[b] == 1 else str(d[b]).translate(SUPS)) for b in BASE if d.get(b)]
    return " ".join(parts) or "1 (dimensionless)"


def dim_check(lhs, rhs, units, local):
    missing = sorted(set(local) - set(units) - {"sin", "sqrt", "pi"})
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"no unit for {missing}")
    terms = sp.Add.make_args(sp.expand(lhs - rhs))
    ds = [dims(t, units, local) for t in terms]
    ok = len(terms) >= 2 and all(d == ds[0] for d in ds)
    return ok, [fmt(d) for d in ds]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- derivations
t, tau, x, y, z, w, v0, a, m, g, h, k, L, r, om = sp.symbols("t tau x y z w v0 a m g h k L r omega", positive=True)


def residual(lhs, rhs, subs):
    return sp.simplify((lhs - rhs).subs(subs))


def derivations(cid, lhs, rhs, S):
    """Return (description, residual) or None. S: the card's symbols by name."""
    if cid == "velocity-constant-acceleration":
        vt = S["v0"] + sp.integrate(S["a"], (tau, 0, S["t"]))
        return "v(t) = v₀ + ∫₀ᵗ a dτ with a constant", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["v"]: vt})
    if cid == "displacement-constant-acceleration":
        st = sp.integrate(S["v0"] + S["a"] * tau, (tau, 0, S["t"]))
        return "s(t) = ∫₀ᵗ (v₀ + aτ) dτ", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["s"]: st})
    if cid == "velocity-displacement":
        vt, st = S["v0"] + S["a"] * t, S["v0"] * t + S["a"] * t**2 / 2
        return "v = v₀ + at and s = v₀t + at²/2 substituted, for all t", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["v"]: vt, S["s"]: st})
    if cid == "kinetic-energy":
        work = sp.integrate(S["m"] * w, (w, 0, S["v"]))
        return "work–energy: Eₖ = ∫F ds = ∫ m (dv/dt) v dt = ∫₀ᵛ m w dw", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["Ek"]: work})
    if cid == "potential-energy":
        work = sp.integrate(S["m"] * S["g"], (y, 0, S["h"]))
        return "work against the weight mg when lifting from 0 to h: ∫₀ʰ mg dy", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["Ep"]: work})
    if cid == "centripetal-force":
        R = sp.Matrix([r * sp.cos(om * t), r * sp.sin(om * t)])
        acc = sp.simplify(sp.sqrt(sum(c**2 for c in R.diff(t, 2))))
        spd = sp.simplify(sp.sqrt(sum(c**2 for c in R.diff(t))))
        sub = {S["F"]: S["m"] * acc.subs({r: S["r"]})}
        res = sp.simplify((lhs - rhs).subs(sub).subs(S["v"], spd.subs({r: S["r"]})))
        return "uniform circular motion r(t) = r(cos ωt, sin ωt): F = m|r″|, v = |r′|", res
    if cid == "pendulum-period":
        th = sp.Function("th")
        sol = sp.dsolve(S["L"] * th(t).diff(t, 2) + S["g"] * th(t), th(t)).rhs  # small-angle sin θ ≈ θ
        omega = sp.sqrt(S["g"] / S["L"])
        assert sp.simplify(sol.subs(t, t + 2 * sp.pi / omega) - sol) == 0
        return "small-angle equation Lθ″ = −gθ solved by dsolve; solution periodic with 2π/√(g/L)", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["T"]: 2 * sp.pi / omega})
    if cid == "spring-period":
        xf = sp.Function("xf")
        sol = sp.dsolve(S["m"] * xf(t).diff(t, 2) + S["k"] * xf(t), xf(t)).rhs
        omega = sp.sqrt(S["k"] / S["m"])
        assert sp.simplify(sol.subs(t, t + 2 * sp.pi / omega) - sol) == 0
        return "mx″ = −kx solved by dsolve; solution periodic with 2π/√(k/m)", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["T"]: 2 * sp.pi / omega})
    if cid == "hydrostatic-pressure":
        Ab = sp.Symbol("A_base", positive=True)
        col = S["rho"] * Ab * S["h"] * S["g"] / Ab
        return "weight of the liquid column ρ·(A·h)·g divided by its base area A", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["p"]: col})
    if cid == "archimedes-principle":
        Ab, Hh, d = sp.symbols("A_base H_box d_top", positive=True)
        p = lambda depth: S["rho"] * S["g"] * depth
        Fb = (p(d + Hh) - p(d)) * Ab
        return "box of base A and height H, top at depth d: (p(d+H) − p(d))·A with p = ρg·depth, V = A·H", \
            residual(lhs, rhs, {S["F"]: Fb, S["V"]: Ab * Hh})
    if cid == "resistors-in-series":
        I, U1 = sp.symbols("I_c U_tot", positive=True)
        Utot = I * S["R1"] + I * S["R2"]
        return "same current I through both: R = (IR₁ + IR₂)/I", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["R"]: Utot / I})
    if cid == "resistors-in-parallel":
        U = sp.Symbol("U_c", positive=True)
        Itot = U / S["R1"] + U / S["R2"]
        return "same voltage U over both, currents add: R = U/(U/R₁ + U/R₂)", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["R"]: U / Itot})
    if cid == "snells-law":
        a1, b1, d, c0 = sp.symbols("a1 b1 d c0", positive=True)
        n1, n2 = S["n1"], S["n2"]
        travel = n1 / c0 * sp.sqrt(x**2 + a1**2) + n2 / c0 * sp.sqrt((d - x)**2 + b1**2)
        dt = sp.diff(travel, x)
        sin1 = x / sp.sqrt(x**2 + a1**2)
        sin2 = (d - x) / sp.sqrt((d - x)**2 + b1**2)
        # stationary travel time (Fermat): dt/dx = 0  <=>  n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2
        res = sp.simplify(c0 * dt - (lhs - rhs).subs({sp.sin(S["theta1"]): sin1, sp.sin(S["theta2"]): sin2}))
        return "Fermat: c·d(travel time)/dx = n₁ sin θ₁ − n₂ sin θ₂ for a ray from (0, a) to (d, −b) via (x, 0)", res
    if cid == "electric-power":
        tt = sp.Symbol("t_c", positive=True)
        P = (S["I"] * tt) * S["U"] / tt
        return "P = W/t with W = QU (voltage = energy per charge) and Q = It", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["P"]: P})
    if cid == "force-on-current-carrying-conductor":
        n, q, vd, Ac = sp.symbols("n_c q_c v_d A_c", positive=True)
        Ftot = (n * Ac * S["L"]) * q * vd * S["B"]
        return "N = nAL carriers of charge q at drift speed v_d, each qv_dB; I = nqv_dA", \
            residual(lhs, rhs, {S["F"]: Ftot, S["I"]: n * q * vd * Ac})
    if cid == "wave-speed":
        T = sp.Symbol("T_c", positive=True)
        return "the wave advances one wavelength λ per period T = 1/f", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["v"]: S["lam"] / T, S["f"]: 1 / T})
    if cid == "de-broglie-wavelength":
        f, c0 = sp.symbols("f_c c_c", positive=True)
        return "consistency for a photon: λ = c/f, p = E/c, E = hf", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["lam"]: c0 / f, S["p"]: S["h"] * f / c0})
    if cid == "weight":
        return "Newton's second law F = ma with a = g", residual(lhs, rhs, {S["F"]: S["m"] * S["g"]})
    return None


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- run
def main():
    d = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())
    results, fails = {}, 0
    for c in d["cards"]:
        cid, back = c["id"], c["back"]["zxx"]
        lhs, rhs, local = parse_back(back)
        S = {k: v for k, v in local.items() if isinstance(v, sp.Symbol)}
        ok, ds = dim_check(lhs, rhs, UNITS[cid], S)
        der = derivations(cid, lhs, rhs, S)
        dres = None if der is None else (der[1] == 0)
        results[cid] = {"back": back, "parsed": f"{sp.sstr(lhs)} = {sp.sstr(rhs)}", "dimensions_ok": ok,
                        "term_dimensions": ds, "derivation": None if der is None else der[0], "derivation_ok": dres}
        fails += (not ok) + (dres is False)
        print(f"{cid:38} {back:26} dims={'ok' if ok else 'FAIL'} [{' | '.join(ds)}]"
              + ("" if der is None else f"  derivation={'ok' if dres else 'FAIL'}"))
    # negative controls
    controls = [
        ("kinetic-energy", "Eₖ = mv", "dims"), ("pendulum-period", "T = 2π√(g/L)", "dims"),
        ("gravitation", "F = Gm₁m₂/r", "dims"), ("mass-energy-equivalence", "E = mc", "dims"),
        ("stefan-boltzmann-law", "P = σAT³", "dims"), ("coulombs-law", "F = kQ₁Q₂/r", "dims"),
        ("kinetic-energy", "Eₖ = mv²", "derivation"), ("displacement-constant-acceleration", "s = v₀t + at²", "derivation"),
        ("resistors-in-parallel", "R = R₁ + R₂", "derivation"), ("spring-period", "T = 2π√(k/m)", "dims"),
        ("snells-law", "n₁ sin θ₂ = n₂ sin θ₁", "derivation"),
    ]
    neg = []
    for cid, wrong, kind in controls:
        lhs, rhs, local = parse_back(wrong)
        S = {k: v for k, v in local.items() if isinstance(v, sp.Symbol)}
        if kind == "dims":
            caught = not dim_check(lhs, rhs, UNITS[cid], S)[0]
        else:
            caught = derivations(cid, lhs, rhs, S)[1] != 0
        neg.append({"card": cid, "wrong": wrong, "check": kind, "caught": caught})
        fails += not caught
        print(f"negative control {wrong:22} ({kind}): {'caught' if caught else 'NOT CAUGHT'}")
    # a limitation, recorded: a wrong numeric factor passes the dimensional check
    lhs, rhs, local = parse_back("Eₖ = mv²")
    S = {k: v for k, v in local.items() if isinstance(v, sp.Symbol)}
    lim = dim_check(lhs, rhs, UNITS["kinetic-energy"], S)[0]
    print(f"limitation: 'Eₖ = mv²' passes the dimensional check: {lim}")
    (H / "verify_results.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"sympy": sp.__version__, "cards": results, "negative_controls": neg, "factor_passes_dims": lim},
        ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    n_der = sum(1 for r_ in results.values() if r_["derivation"])
    print(f"{len(results)} cards: dimensions ok {sum(r_['dimensions_ok'] for r_ in results.values())}; "
          f"derivations {n_der}, ok {sum(1 for r_ in results.values() if r_['derivation_ok'])}; failures {fails}")
    sys.exit(1 if fails else 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

## Quality control

7 rounds, 39 findings: 27 fixed, 1 rejected after checking, 11 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (102 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Machine verification (SymPy dimensions and derivations), source cross-checks (OpenStax, Wikidata, Swedish Wikipedia), licences, symbols and Swedish terms (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 42 cards, the sources and the deck metadata

verify_physics.py (SymPy 1.14.0) parsed every back from the dossier and found all 42 dimensionally consistent in SI units; 18 cards also passed a derivation from first principles, and all 11 deliberately wrong equations used as negative controls failed as they must. Every card's equation agrees with OpenStax University Physics (up to symbols and rearrangement), 27 with a Wikidata defining formula and 39 with a Swedish Wikipedia article; every quote was checked by script to occur verbatim in the saved source. The builder's 102 Wikidata checks (labels, aliases and quantity symbols) pass; one planned label check was left out for a typographic difference (Stefan–Boltzmann). Discrepancies and decisions are logged below.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| ohms-law | The brief describes OpenStax University Physics as CC BY 4.0, but every OpenStax page fetched and the archive records of all three volumes give CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 ("Textbook content produced by OpenStax is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike License"). | OpenStax is recorded as all-rights-reserved (the builder has no identifier for a non-commercial licence) and used for verification only; nothing was taken from it, so the deck stays CC0. | fixed |
| ohms-law | Voltage: Swedish schools and Wikidata's first quantity symbol write U, OpenStax and many English texts V ("V=IR"); a back in no language must use one symbol for both languages. | U throughout (Ohm's law, electric power, capacitance), named on every front; the Ohm's law note gives the English form V = IR, and the description says so. | fixed |
| force-on-current-carrying-conductor | OpenStax and Swedish texts write the conductor's length as a lower-case l, which in "F = BIl" is easily read as a second capital I (the current). | Every length is a capital L (pendulum, resistivity, conductor), named on the front. | fixed |
| stefan-boltzmann-law | Wikidata's English label of Q704747 is "Stefan-Boltzmann law" with a hyphen; the card writes the en dash of a law named after two people, as the Swedish label "Stefan–Boltzmanns lag" and the English Wikipedia sitelink "Stefan–Boltzmann law" do.
